title: ML-MT125-MtLifecycleBoardGui

scope.summary:
GOAL: Give the operator (and observing models) a live MT lifecycle board — the visual surface over the MT-123 run state machine and MT-124 validation handoff. Two surfaces: (1) a native egui pane in handshake_native alongside the existing swarm lane diagnostics; (2) an extension of the legacy-React SwarmBoard/SessionWorkbench (the currently-shipping swarm operator surface) so the board is usable before native parity closure. Per-MT-run rows with drill-down into the owning session, steer/interrupt entry, and validation status. AccessKit semantics + Argus verification are mandatory (GUI MT).

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New native pane src/frontend/handshake_native/src/mt_lifecycle_board.rs registered next to swarm_lane_diagnostics.rs; extensions to app/src/components/swarm/SwarmBoard.tsx and app/src/components/swarm/SessionWorkbench.tsx (named GUI-surface exception to the app/src/** freeze); thin read API/IPC binding if the MT-123 list_runs surface is not yet exposed over the session API (MT-007). No new backend business logic.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Data source — MT-run rows come from MT-123 list_runs (via the MT-007 session API route surface) and update EVENT-DRIVEN from the MT-009 bus state-change events (native: existing event subscription seam; React: the existing swarm event push channel used by SwarmBoard). NO periodic refresh timer polling the backend: updates arrive on events; a manual refresh button is allowed.
2. Row model (both surfaces render the same typed row): mt_id, wp_id, run state (typed badge: DISPATCHED/CLAIMED/IMPLEMENTING/SIGNALED{kind}/VALIDATION_HANDOFF/VALIDATED/FAILED/BLOCKED), worker session_id + model lane, workspace (session worktree path and, when VM-bound, the worktree_vm binding indicator), last signal kind + received-at, blocker kind + detail when BLOCKED, failure reason when FAILED (incl. SignalParseFailure indicator), validation status (open handoff receipt / closure verdict / closer attribution from MT-124 receipts), and run lineage (prior run_ids for the same mt_id, append-only history).
3. Drill-down — activating a row opens the owning session in the session tree / SessionWorkbench (existing session-detail surface); from there the operator reaches transcript, FR records, and the workspace path. The board does NOT duplicate the workbench; it links.
4. Steer/interrupt entry — each non-terminal row exposes Steer and Interrupt actions routed through the EXISTING steer-queue/session-control surfaces (MT-002 steer queue via MT-007 session API). The board is an entry point only: it submits to those surfaces and renders their acknowledgement; it owns no steering logic.
5. States of the board itself — empty state ('no MT runs'), backend-unreachable state (typed error banner, no silent blank), and stale-event state (last-event timestamp shown so the operator can judge freshness without the app polling).
6. Accessibility/automation — native pane: AccessKit node per row and per action button with stable ids (mt-run-row-{run_id}, mt-run-steer-{run_id}, mt-run-interrupt-{run_id}, mt-run-open-session-{run_id}); React: data-testid with the same id scheme. These stable ids are the parallel-model interaction contract (GLOBAL-BUILD-040).
7. Argus — native pane verified via the canonical Argus flow: AccessKit tree inspection (rows + actions present), screenshot/snapshot reference, layout-overlap check, console/renderer error scan. React extension verified via the project's existing web GUI check path for SwarmBoard.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read swarm_lane_diagnostics.rs (pane registration, event subscription, AccessKit id conventions) and SwarmBoard.tsx/SessionWorkbench.tsx (row rendering, push-channel subscription, drill-down wiring) in the product worktree.
2. Expose list_runs + receipts over the MT-007 route surface if not already exposed (thin read-only route; no new business logic) and add the matching typed frontend client calls.
3. Implement the native pane: row table, badges, drill-down link, steer/interrupt entry, empty/unreachable/stale states, AccessKit ids.
4. Extend SwarmBoard.tsx with the MT-run section + SessionWorkbench.tsx with the per-run detail block (last signal, receipts, lineage); reuse existing components/styles; data-testids.
5. Native tests (egui harness per crate convention) for row rendering per state, action-event emission, and AccessKit id stability; React tests per app test convention for row rendering + drill-down.
6. Run Argus verification on the native pane and record evidence; run the React GUI check; run proof targets.
allowed_paths: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/** (pane registration seams only — shell/menu wiring)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/** (thin read-only route exposure for list_runs/receipts ONLY if MT-007/MT-123 did not already expose it)
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (except the two named GUI surfaces above — no other legacy React edits)
.GOV/** (the product READS MT contracts; it never writes .GOV)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/mt_run_state.rs (business logic frozen; read via API only)
acceptance_criteria: Native egui MT lifecycle board pane exists, registered alongside swarm lane diagnostics, rendering per-run rows with state badge, worker session, workspace (worktree/VM indicator), last signal, blocker/failure detail, validation status, and lineage.
React SwarmBoard shows the MT-run section and SessionWorkbench shows the per-run detail block, rendering the same typed row model.
Board updates are event-driven from the MT-009 bus push channels; grep-level proof that the board code contains no periodic backend-status polling timer; manual refresh only.
Row drill-down opens the owning session in the existing session tree/workbench surface (link, not duplication).
Steer and Interrupt actions on non-terminal rows submit through the existing steer-queue/session-control surfaces and render acknowledgement; terminal rows offer no such actions.
Empty, backend-unreachable, and stale-event states render explicitly — no silent blank pane.
AccessKit nodes (native) and data-testids (React) use the stable id scheme mt-run-row-{run_id} / mt-run-steer-{run_id} / mt-run-interrupt-{run_id} / mt-run-open-session-{run_id} — asserted by test.
Argus evidence recorded for the native pane: AccessKit tree with rows+actions, screenshot/snapshot reference, layout-overlap check, renderer/console error scan; React GUI check evidence recorded.
cargo build (native) and app build green; new tests green.
proof_targets: rg -n "set_interval|setInterval|poll" src/frontend/handshake_native/src/mt_lifecycle_board.rs app/src/components/swarm/SwarmBoard.tsx -i | rg -v "// no-poll" | wc -l | grep -q '^0'
argus inspect --target mt_lifecycle_board (per the canonical Argus invocation in the product worktree; record tree + snapshot evidence)
expected_tests: native row rendering across all run states incl. blocker/failure/parse-failure detail
steer/interrupt action emission + absence on terminal rows
implementation_notes: This is the productized successor of the operator's terminal-window juggling: the board is training ground for in-app session display (operator feedback: terminal hygiene / future in-app session display). Keep the row model in one shared typed definition per surface so native and React cannot drift silently.
The stale-event indicator exists BECAUSE polling is forbidden: freshness is communicated by showing when the last event arrived, not by re-querying on a timer.

SwarmBoard/SessionWorkbench are the ONLY legacy-React files touchable here (named exception); if the extension pressures other app/src files, stop and surface it rather than widening scope — the legacy notes-editor removal discipline elsewhere in WP-017 depends on app/src staying frozen.
Reuse swarm_lane_diagnostics.rs event-subscription and pane conventions verbatim; the board is a sibling pane, not a fork of the diagnostics pane.
Steer entry submits to the MT-002 steer queue exactly as the workbench does — if the workbench steer control is componentized, reuse that component.

surfaces: native egui: mt_lifecycle_board pane (new, registered alongside swarm_lane_diagnostics)
argus_targets: mt_lifecycle_board pane AccessKit tree (rows + steer/interrupt/open-session actions)
layout-overlap + renderer error scan on the pane

target_entries: MT lifecycle board: reading run states, blockers, validation status
Steering/interrupting a dispatched MT worker from the board
Drilling into a worker session from an MT run row

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.obligation: The board renders the mt_runs structured state verbatim (states, blockers, receipts) — no board-local derived truth.
Drill-down reaches transcript/FR trace surfaces for every run; stale-event timestamp exposes event-flow health.
This MT IS the operator surface for the ML family; Argus + UserManual evidence required in the same change.

risk_if_missed: The MT loop runs headless: the operator cannot see run states, blockers, or validation status without reading PG/logs — UI confusion and invisible stuck runs, violating the observable/attributable/recoverable bar.

risks: RISK-1: The board quietly reintroduces polling (refresh timer) to feel live, violating the operator's no-polling rule at the GUI layer.
RISK-2: Board-local state derivation (computing 'done' from signals client-side) drifts from mt_runs canonical state — UI count vs backend truth divergence (GLOBAL-SOT-026 class).
RISK-3: Steer/interrupt from the board bypasses the sanctioned steer-queue/session-control path and mutates sessions directly.
RISK-4: Unstable row/action identifiers break parallel-model automation and Argus regression comparisons across runs.
RISK-5: Backend-unreachable or event-channel-dead renders as an empty board, indistinguishable from 'no runs' — operator misreads system health.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): event-driven updates + manual refresh only; no-polling grep proof target; stale-event timestamp is the freshness mechanism.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): rows render backend-typed state verbatim; no client-side state inference; test asserts badge==backend state for every state kind.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): board actions submit through the existing steer-queue/session-control surfaces only; no direct session mutation API in board code — asserted by review + test.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): stable id scheme keyed by run_id, asserted by AccessKit/data-testid tests.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): distinct typed empty vs unreachable vs stale states, each with its own rendering test.

research_provenance.source: WP-017 stub research basis (SwarmControlRoom/SessionWorkbench GUI extension direction; VS Code Comment/board UI contracts as reference) + verified product code: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/swarm_lane_diagnostics.rs, app/src/components/swarm/SwarmBoard.tsx, app/src/components/swarm/SessionWorkbench.tsx + HBR visual-debug obligations (Argus/AccessKit conventions in the product worktree).
corrections: Both surfaces (native pane + legacy React swarm board) are in scope because SwarmBoard is the shipping operator surface while native parity is still closing; the React touch is confined to the two named files as an explicit exception.
Freshness is event-timestamp-based, not poll-based — the no-polling operator rule applies to the GUI, not just the backend.
